title: Audit Log Evidence Playbook for Customer Assessments
body:
Purpose:
This playbook is a concise operational guide for preparing audit-log artifacts and SIEM exports to respond to customer security questionnaires and assessments. It focuses on what evidence to collect, how to annotate exports for reviewers, and how to tie artifacts back to RBAC v2 controls and the audit log schema used by Redwood Inference.

Intended audience:
- Customer security reviewers
- Redwood security engineers and evidence owners
- Solutions engineers preparing demos and artifact bundles for SOC2/enterprise prospects

High-level approach:
1) Map questionnaire/control to artifact types (logs, config snapshots, screenshots, procedures).
2) Extract targeted logs and SIEM exports with time-window and correlation IDs.
3) Produce a short narrative per artifact explaining scope and trust boundaries.
4) Redact PII and sensitive tokens; keep integrity checks (hashes) for each file.
5) Provide a minimal reproducer (query or CLI command) so reviewers can verify the export.

Common control mappings (examples):
- Access control and RBAC (RBAC v2): provide role definitions, assignment history snapshot, and audit events showing role grants/revocations.
- Privileged actions and admin operations: provide admin operation logs (user management, key rotations) with before/after state snapshots.
- Data access / exfiltration controls: provide object access logs, copy/download events, and network egress summary from the SIEM.
- System changes and deployments: provide CI/CD audit events and model rollouts with rollbacks included.

Recommended artifact set per assessment request (small, medium, large):
- Small (Q&A / quick proof): 1–3 targeted log exports + RBAC role list + narrative.
- Medium (detailed questionnaire): 24–72 hour SIEM export for scoped services + role change history + configuration snapshots + query used to generate export.
- Large (in-depth audit / on-site review): full-day export around incident windows, system config backups, signed hashes, and runbook excerpts.

Audit log schema (canonical fields we include in exports):
Timestamp | RequestID | Actor (user_id) | ActorRole | Action | ResourceType | ResourceID | Outcome | SourceIP | Region | Service | TraceID | Extra (json blob)
2024-10-01T12:23:45Z | req_8f3a | user_238 | platform-admin | role.grant | user | user_239 | success | 34.72.11.9 | us-east1 | console | trace_abc123 | {"reason":"onboarding"}

Notes on schema usage:
- ActorRole reflects RBAC v2 computed role at time of event (not the role assignment state).
- TraceID correlates request path through front-end, API gateway, and serving runtime.
- Extra is a small JSON blob for non-standard fields (e.g., feature flags, ephemeral session ids). Keep it small to avoid SIEM ingestion costs.

SIEM export best practices:
- Provide the exact SIEM query (and saved query ID) used to create the export.
- Include the time window and any sampling or rate-limit notes.
- If using compressed exports (gzip/ndjson), include instructions to decompress and a checksum.
- Annotate the exported file name with the time window and scope (e.g., auth-events_us-east1_20240911-20240912.ndjson.gz).

RBAC v2-specific evidence tips:
- Provide canonical role definitions (JSON/YAML) and a human-readable mapping of which permissions map to which API endpoints.
- Export role assignment history: who granted what to whom and the approver (if applicable).
- For ephemeral elevation (just-in-time): include the JIT request record and the linked justification/audit ID.
- Show one example where a role change prevents an action (negative test) and include the corresponding audit event.

Redaction and privacy:
- Replace email addresses with hashed identifiers in shared artifacts (sha256(user@example.com)).
- Remove or mask full JWTs, API keys, private keys. Keep authorization headers out of exports.
- When a PII-heavy event is required, submit a secure review request and provide a limited redacted view.

Packaging checklist (deliverable to customer):
- README.txt with summary of files and scope (who generated, time window, queries used).
- audit_manifest.csv: list of files, sha256, generator command, brief description.
- SIEM exports (ndjson or csv) with saved query snippet in a .sql/.kql file.
- Config snapshots: RBAC roles (json), IAM policies (json), and service-config.yaml.
- Narrative per control linking artifacts to questionnaire sections.
- Signed statement from evidence owner (name, role, email) confirming completeness.

Example CLI snippet to pull targeted events (internal SIEM):
# fetch auth events for user_238 in last 7d
redwood-siem query "event.type:auth AND actor.id:user_238" --from 2024-09-30T00:00:00Z --to 2024-10-07T00:00:00Z --output ndjson > user_238_auth_20240930-20241007.ndjson

Narrative template (short):
- Control: "Restrict admin role assignment"
- Artifact: roles_v2_snapshot_20240930.json; role_assignment_history_20240901-20241001.ndjson
- Why this answers the control: role grant events show only platform-admin approvers applied via the console; JIT elevation events are logged and require an approver ticket.
- How to validate: run the provided SIEM query and confirm that role.grant events show an approver field and that the ActorRole matches computed role.

Operational notes for internal owners:
- Keep a rotating evidence owner list per product area. Owners must be able to produce a 72-hour export within 48 hours.
- Maintain a library of sanitized example exports for quick demo purposes.
- Automate manifest and checksum generation as part of evidence packaging pipelines (see linked GitHub PR).

Frequently asked questions:
Q: How much historical log data do we provide?
A: Default is 90 days for high-level audit events. For deeper audits, provide the narrower window requested by the customer. Avoid unbounded exports.

Q: Do we share raw SIEM access?
A: No. We provide exports and saved queries plus a walkthrough. Direct SIEM access is available under enterprise private deployments with separate contracts.

Q: Who signs the evidence?
A: The named evidence owner (usually a senior engineer or security lead) and the product security manager.

Appendix — quick sample manifest (CSV format):
file_name,sha256,command,description
roles_v2_snapshot_20240930.json,3a7b...e9f,redwood-config fetch roles --date 2024-09-30,Canonical RBAC v2 definitions at snapshot
user_238_auth_20240930-20241007.ndjson,c12f...0aa,redwood-siem query "event.type:auth AND actor.id:user_238" --from 2024-09-30 --to 2024-10-07,Targeted auth events for user_238

Contact and escalation:
Primary evidence owner: Aisha Patel (security engineer) — aisha.patel@redwood.com
Escalation: Security on-call (pager duty link in Confluence)

Last updated: 2024-11-02

Note: This is a working playbook intended for internal use and customer-facing evidence bundles. Use it as a baseline and adjust per-customer contractual and compliance requirements.
